newsitem.title: ITALY: EU accession talks must all start at once - Italy.
newsitem.headline: EU accession talks must all start at once - Italy.

text.p: A junior Italian foreign minister said on Wednesday that negotiations with candidates wishing to join the European Union should start simultaneously.
"We must distinguish between the enlargement of the European Union and the enlargement of NATO," Piero Fassino said.

"On the enlargement of the European Union, the Italian position is that negotiations must be started simultaneously with all candidates and that at the end of the negotiations, the timing (for EU entry) would be worked out," he said.
"On the enlargement of NATO, we maintain that the enlargement must include Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic and also Slovenia and Romania."
Fassino made his remarks in a telephone call to Reuters a day after a visit to Bucharest where he reiterated Italy's support for Romania to join NATO.

An official statement, in Romanian, from the office of President Emil Constantinescu after talks between the two men on Tuesday had quoted Fassino as saying Italy favoured a "simultaneous beginning of talks between NATO and all candidates" for the Alliance's first eastward expansion.

The statement had quoted him as saying that such an approach would "avoid feelings of exclusion or frustration which might endanger the development of emerging democracies in eastern and Central Europe".
A NATO summit in Madrid in July is expected to kick off the process of enlargement.
Romania is lobbying for support for first-wave admission to NATO, alongside more developed east Europeans Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, viewed as near-certain entrants.

Constantinescu, whose centrists removed ex-communists from office in elections last November, is spearheading the drive to gain Western support for his country's foremost foreign policy goal of integration into NATO and the European Union.
"NATO's southern flank members have perfectly understood the advantages of our country's geo-strategic position," he told reporters after the talks with Fassino.
